sections.title: Housing prices in Mid and East Antrim
sections.standfirst: How average house prices and rents are changing in Mid and East Antrim.
sections.label: You have selected Mid and East Antrim but you can choose a different local authority in the UK below.

sections.content:
The average house price in Mid and East Antrim was £177,000 in April 2026 to June 2026 (provisional), up 8.2% from April 2025 to June 2025. This was lower than the rise in Northern Ireland (9.2%) over the same period.

Go to house price section ↓

Rent data for Northern Ireland are for 'broad rental market areas'. Mid and East Antrim falls within the rental area of Lough Neagh Upper.

The average private rent price in Lough Neagh Upper was £797 in May 2026. That compares with £875 across Northern Ireland as a whole.

Go to rents section ↓
Local housing data are based on a smaller number of properties than our national estimates, meaning short-term trends are more variable. We advise looking at trends over a year or longer.

We regularly revise our house prices estimates. UK-level rent estimates for the latest two months, and all house price data, are provisional and subject to revision.

Figures in this article are not seasonally adjusted.

Northern Ireland rents data are entirely for advertised new lets. This is a different method to other UK nations. See the More data on the housing market section for further details on comparability.

sections.title: Average house price in Mid and East Antrim was £177,000 in April 2026 to June 2026
sections.content: The provisional average house price in Mid and East Antrim in April 2026 to June 2026 was £177,000. This was higher than the average of £164,000 in April 2025 to June 2025 (revised), a 8.2% rise.

sections.content:
Across Northern Ireland, the average house price in April 2026 to June 2026 was £202,000, which was more than a year earlier (£185,000).

Across the UK, a home sold for an average of £272,000 in June 2026, which was up slightly from the June 2025 average of £267,000.

sections.title: Average private rents rose in Lough Neagh Upper
sections.content: Mid and East Antrim falls within the rental area of Lough Neagh Upper.

sections.title: Average private rental price in Lough Neagh Upper rental market area, May 2026

sections.content: Private rents in Lough Neagh Upper averaged at £797 a month in May 2026. This was an increase from £776 in May 2025, a 2.7% rise.

Across Northern Ireland, the average monthly rent was £875, up from £855 a year earlier.

Across the UK, the average rent price in May 2026 was £1,383, which was up from £1,339 in May 2025.

sections.content:
By how many bedrooms there are in a property, average rents as of May 2026 in Lough Neagh Upper rental area were:

  • One bedroom: £562
  • Two bedrooms: £706
  • Three bedrooms: £803
  • Four or more bedrooms: £1,088

Taking the data instead by property type, average rents were:

  • Flats and maisonettes: £710
  • Terraced properties: £745
  • Semi-detached properties: £837
  • Detached properties: £959

sections.title: More data on the housing market
sections.content:
This article is regularly updated with the most recent rents and house prices information. The full time series for rental prices can be found in our associated data releases. The full time series for house prices can be found in the UK House Price Index reports on gov.uk.

You can also read our most recent Private rent and house prices bulletin.

The methods used to produce the rental prices can be found in the Price Index of Private Rents Quality and Methodology Information. The methods used to produce the house prices can be found in the House Price Index Quality and Methodology Information.

Northern Ireland rents data are provided for broad rental market areas, which cover a set of postcodes. Some local government districts in Northern Ireland overlap with several of these rental areas.

To get a best match of local authority to rental area, we looked at the proportion of postcodes per local authority that fell within each rental area. We exclude marginal matches, for clarity (where fewer than 1% of postcodes overlap).

sections.title: About this article
sections.content:
The content in this article is generated using semi-automated journalism, based on rules pre-programmed by Office for National Statistics (ONS) staff.

This is a new product in Beta release, intended to improve the accessibility of housing market data at local level. Send us feedback about this page or contact the Housing Market Indices team by emailing hpi@ons.gov.uk.

Articles are not available for Isles of Scilly and City of London, as the survey samples of the resident population are too small.
